question: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of painless lesions on his face that he has had since shortly after birth. They recently moved to the USA from Indonesia where they had limited access to healthcare. A photograph of the lesions is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The painless lesions on the boy's face that have been present since shortly after birth suggest a vascular lesion. Infantile hemangiomas are common benign tumors of infancy that typically appear shortly after birth and can be painless. Given the age of the child and the description of the lesions, infantile hemangioma is the most likely diagnosis. Other options like verruca vulgaris (warts) and molluscum contagiosum are usually not present at birth and have different characteristics. Neurofibromas typically appear later in life and are associated with neurofibromatosis. Spider angiomas are usually seen in adults and are not congenital. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is infantile hemangioma.
